name: TiKV
summary: A distributed transactional key-value store that partitions ordered keys into Regions, replicates each Region with Raft, stores data locally in RocksDB, and exposes raw and transactional APIs.

features.name: Region-sharded ordered keyspace
features.description: TiKV treats storage as an ordered key-value map partitioned into contiguous left-closed, right-open Regions; Regions are the unit of movement, distribution, and replication.
benefits: Supports horizontal capacity and range-oriented scans
Provides a bounded unit for scheduling, replication, and rebalancing
costs: Hot keys and uneven Region sizes require scheduling and splitting
Clients and control-plane metadata must locate the relevant Region

features.name: Raft-replicated Regions
features.description: Each Region has replicas forming a Raft group; writes pass through Raft log replication and become durable after the group reaches the required majority, rather than writing directly to RocksDB.
benefits: Provides failure-tolerant replicated state with leader election
Separates consensus ordering from local engine persistence
costs: Majority quorum and leader coordination add write latency
Replica repair, membership, and log management consume resources

features.name: MVCC transactional API
features.description: TiKV offers raw single-key and transactional multi-key APIs; the transactional model uses MVCC versions and Percolator-inspired locking to provide ACID distributed transactions and snapshot isolation.
benefits: Offers a clear choice between raw access and multi-key transactions
Allows readers at earlier logical times to observe prior versions
costs: Locks, versions, and distributed commit add storage and coordination state
Transaction behavior requires explicit handling of conflicts and liveness

mathematical_views.question: How does an ordered keyspace partition into Region intervals while preserving lookup, scan, and movement boundaries?
assumptions: Region intervals are non-overlapping and cover the modeled keyspace
Region metadata identifies the replica group serving each interval
The view abstracts local RocksDB file layout

mathematical_views.question: How do Raft-ordered mutations and MVCC timestamps produce durable, snapshot-isolated transactional observations?
assumptions: A committed Raft log is the authoritative order for a Region
MVCC version selection follows the transaction timestamp rules
The view abstracts network timing and recovery implementation details

costs: Region placement, splitting, and hotspot management add control-plane work

benefits: Quorum durability and automatic replica failover
costs: Consensus traffic and quorum availability constrain write throughput

benefits: Snapshot reads and multi-key ACID semantics
costs: Version retention, locks, and conflict resolution increase complexity
